column5: As a customer in a queue, I want the team to know the real time from palm scan to result so it can fix the slowest part of checkout.
column13: Report includes median, p95 and failure rate for at least 20 sandbox attempts.
column17: Measure median, p95 and failure rate across at least 20 sandbox attempts using instrumented stages.
column19: Journey: waiting time. Measured prototype performance informs improvements and honest expectations; it does not turn an assumed one-to-three-second charge time into a proven end-to-end promise.

column4: Draft privacy notice, consent record and DPIA checklist
column5: As a customer deciding whether to enroll, I want a clear privacy notice and an accountable review of biometric risks, not an unexplained consent checkbox.
column13: Prototype documentation is review-ready; live use remains blocked until legal/compliance approval.
column17: Prepare the privacy notice, consent record and DPIA review checklist using the agreed policy and threat model.
column19: Journey: informed trust. The documentation explains the prototype’s handling and rights process; a draft checklist is not legal approval, and live use remains gated on required review.

column4: Run MVP acceptance review and cut non-critical defects
column5: As a customer trying the month-end demo, I want the core journey to work safely even if optional polish must wait.
column13: All critical tests pass or have an explicit blocker/owner; stretch work is deferred.
column17: Review critical acceptance evidence, assign unresolved blockers and defer non-critical enhancements.
column19: Journey: release decision. Enrollment, correct charging, isolation and reconciliation take priority; unresolved critical defects are visible rather than hidden by a completion claim.

column4: Freeze release candidate and production-like test configuration
column5: As a demo operator, I want the tested version to remain stable between rehearsal and presentation instead of changing unexpectedly overnight.
column13: Release is tagged; secrets/config are documented and no new features enter.
column17: Tag a release candidate and freeze documented, production-like test configuration without adding new features.
column19: Journey: repeatable demonstration. The same known build and test settings are used each time; production-like configuration does not authorize real payments or commercial use.

column4: Run five consecutive end-to-end demo payments
column5: As a merchant considering the prototype, I want several consecutive customers to complete the demo, not just one carefully rescued attempt.
column13: Five attempts succeed without manual database changes or duplicate charges.
column17: Run five consecutive end-to-end demo payments against the frozen release and record evidence.
column18: Test customer; test merchant; QA team
column19: Journey: repeat checkout. Five successful sandbox attempts without manual data changes or duplicate charges provide repeatability evidence, not a claim of production reliability.

column4: Demonstrate merchant T+1 settlement and reconciliation journey
column5: As a merchant, I want to follow a sale from payment confirmation to expected settlement and reconciliation, including what happens if the numbers differ.
column13: Merchant page explains pending, expected, settled and variance states using sandbox/mock data.
column17: Demonstrate pending, expected, settled and variance states using labeled sandbox or mock data.
column19: Journey: explain settlement. The merchant can distinguish an estimate from processor-reported status and a mismatch; simulated settlement is never described as an actual bank payout.

column4: Finalize architecture, API, commissioning, recovery and demo runbook
column5: As a new teammate or terminal operator, I want instructions to set up, activate, demonstrate and recover the prototype without depending on its original builder.
column13: A new teammate can set up and demonstrate the prototype from documentation.
column17: Complete architecture, API, commissioning, recovery and demo runbooks.
column19: Journey: support and handover. A new operator can reproduce setup and follow a recovery procedure when something fails, reducing interruptions for customers at the counter.

column4: Export final CAD, STL, BOM and assembly photos
column5: As a hardware builder, I want the final model, print files, component list and assembly photos so I can reproduce or repair the same terminal.
column13: All fabrication files and component list are archived.
column17: Archive editable CAD, STL, bill of materials and assembly documentation.
column18: Hardware builder; terminal operator; merchant indirectly
column19: Journey: maintain the device. A damaged part can be recreated from the approved design, preserving the tested screen placement and palm-capture geometry.

column4: Record backup video and conduct full dress rehearsal
column5: As someone watching the demo, I want to see the complete customer and merchant story even if the live network fails during the presentation.
column13: Backup video and live script cover enrollment, payment, merchant transaction and settlement.
column17: Rehearse the full script and record a clearly identified backup of the working prototype.
column19: Journey: communicate the result. Enrollment, palm payment, merchant transaction and settlement views form one coherent demonstration; recorded footage is labeled rather than presented as a live transaction.

column4: Sign off prototype completion and post-month roadmap
column5: As a project owner and prospective merchant, I want a clear account of what the prototype proves, what remains incomplete and what must happen before real use.
column13: MVP definition is checked, open blockers are recorded and commercialisation work is separated.
column17: Check completion against scope, record open blockers and separate future commercialisation work from prototype delivery.
column19: Journey: after the demo. Sign-off reflects actual evidence; processor approval, commercial biometric licensing, privacy/security review and remaining reliability work stay explicit next steps.
